presets.guide.standardIntro: Choose Standard mode for everyday coding, file work, research, scripts, and batch processing. Batch work does not require PTC.
presets.guide.standardExplanation: Agent uses its tools directly to read and edit files, search, and run terminal commands. Standard mode includes Skills, planning, goals, subagents, workflows, and context compaction.
presets.guide.standardUsage: Describe the goal, relevant files, limits, and how to verify the result. Example: “Find why the search form loses results after a second submit. Fix it, run the relevant tests, and explain the cause.”
presets.guide.ptcIntro: Choose PTC mode when you want programs to filter, organize, and summarize large tool results.
presets.guide.ptcExplanation: Agent writes a TypeScript program and calls tools through run_code; results go to run_code first, and Agent sees only what the program prints or returns (images are attached separately). The program can filter or combine results, handle per-item errors, and organize suitable calls concurrently. Nested calls remain recorded and subject to tool permissions. The built-in PTC preset leaves the workflow tool disabled.
presets.guide.ptcUsage: Specify the inputs, processing rules, and output format. Example: “Check every JSON file in configs/ against schema.json, report each missing or invalid field to a CSV, include unreadable files, and leave the originals unchanged.”
presets.guide.minimalIntro: Fewer tools do not make a task easier. Choose Minimal mode as a baseline for controlled comparisons.
presets.guide.minimalExplanation: Minimal mode provides one persistent shell tool and a fixed system prompt. It does not load Skills, planning, context compaction, or the standard runtime context. It can still read files and run scripts through terminal commands.
presets.guide.minimalUsage: For a fair comparison, keep the model, permissions, task input, and starting workspace state the same; compare completion, tool calls, and resulting changes separately. Example: “Run the tests, find the cause of the failure, make the smallest fix, and run the relevant tests again.”
presets.guide.cordisIntro: Creator mode helps build custom presets and plugins. The preset applies to new tasks; plugins may need a DSH restart.
presets.guide.cordisExplanation: Creator mode adds runtime inspection, persistent plugin management, and guidance for building Cordis plugins and Agent presets to the standard task tools. A plugin can register services that custom presets combine with tools and instructions for a kind of task. Ask Agent to install and verify the result because some changes need additional activation steps.
presets.guide.cordisUsage: Describe the capability, where it should appear, and how to verify it. Example: “Create a custom mode for reviewing pull requests, with a checklist for correctness, security, and tests. Make it the default for new tasks and explain how to verify it.”
